title: Arbitrary-call facets (Farm/Depot/Tractor) lack nonReentrant guard

location.code_snippet: function farm(bytes[] calldata data) external payable fundsSafu withEth returns (bytes[] memory results) { ... }  // no nonReentrant; LibFarm._farm -> facet.delegatecall(data)

description: Beanstalk's reentrancy defense is a hybrid model: a diamond-wide ReentrancyGuard (shared storage slot s.sys.reentrantStatus) applied to the genuinely sensitive Silo/Convert functions (SiloFacet deposit/withdraw/transfer, ConvertFacet.convert, PipelineConvertFacet.pipelineConvert, EnrootFacet, ClaimFacet, MarketplaceFacet, UnripeFacet.chop) PLUS the Invariable balance/stalk/supply modifiers (fundsSafu, noNetFlow, noOutFlow, oneOutFlow, noSupplyChange/Increase) on everything else. The four general-purpose ARBITRARY EXTERNAL CALL entrypoints that the attack-surface map flags as the prime reentrancy surface -- FarmFacet.farm/advancedFarm, DepotFacet.pipe/multiPipe/advancedPipe/etherPipe, TractorFacet.tractor, and the executeAdvancedFarmCalls window inside LibPipelineConvert -- carry NO nonReentrant modifier (FarmFacet nonReentrant=0, DepotFacet nonReentrant=0, TractorFacet nonReentrant=0). They depend entirely on (a) the shared guard being already set by an outer guarded caller, and (b) the Invariable post-conditions. The architectural consequence: when a user enters through one of these unguarded entrypoints (e.g. FarmFacet.farm or DepotFacet.advancedPipe), the shared reentrant flag is NOT set, so an external call made through Pipeline can re-enter the diamond and reach OTHER unguarded state-mutating functions (FieldFacet.sow/harvest -- 0 guards, SeasonFacet.sunrise/gm -- 0 guards, FertilizerFacet.mintFertilizer/claimFertilized -- 0 guards) while the outer batch is mid-execution. Reentry into a nonReentrant function (any Silo/Convert op) IS correctly blocked by the shared flag once one is active; the gap is the unguarded<->unguarded reentry surface, where the only backstop is the Invariable balance equality/inequality checks evaluated at each modifier's closing brace. Those checks defend token *custody* (balances cannot net-decrease) but do NOT defend internal accounting consistency (stalk attribution, deltaB snapshots, soil/temperature, season state) read mid-batch. This is the structural seam that the economic/oracle reserve-skew vectors (see cross_agent_refs) ride on; on its own it is a Medium reentrancy-surface exposure pending a traced consumer that converts the mid-batch state read into fund loss.
impact: An external call routed through Pipeline/Farm/Depot can re-enter the diamond and reach unguarded state-mutating functions (sow, harvest, sunrise, mintFertilizer) while an outer arbitrary-call batch is mid-execution and internal accounting (stalk/deltaB/season) is transiently inconsistent. Token custody is protected by the Invariable balance modifiers, so direct theft is not demonstrated by reentrancy alone; the realized impact is the enabling seam for the reserve-skew/oracle economic exploits tracked by the flash_loan/oracle/economic agents. Standalone severity Medium (state-read inconsistency, no traced direct drain).

ite.intent: Re-enter Beanstalk through an unguarded arbitrary-call entrypoint to read/act on transiently inconsistent internal accounting (stalk/deltaB/season) before the outer batch finalizes.
ite.technique: Enter via DepotFacet.advancedPipe or FarmFacet.farm (neither sets s.sys.reentrantStatus). Inside Pipeline, craft a PipeCall whose target calls back into FarmFacet.farm -> delegatecall sunrise/sow/mintFertilizer (also unguarded). The shared guard is not active, so the reentry is not blocked; LibFarm._farm executes the reentered function in diamond context.
ite.evasion: Developer intent: Invariable balance modifiers + diamond-wide guard. The gap: the guard is NOT applied to the arbitrary-call entrypoints, so unguarded->unguarded reentry is unblocked; Invariable checks custody (balances) at modifier exit, not transient stalk/deltaB/season accounting consumed mid-batch.

ice_chain.corrupted_state: Transient internal accounting read during an arbitrary-call batch: well reserves / LibDeltaB.currentDeltaB, s.sys.season state, stalk attribution -- none are persistently corrupted, but they are readable in an inconsistent mid-batch state.
ice_chain.consumer_function: PipelineConvertFacet.pipelineConvert stalk-penalty / SeasonFacet.sunrise mint (candidate consumers; manual trace required)
ice_chain.consumer_action: Could mint mispriced BDV/stalk or over-issue sunrise reward Beans if the mid-batch reserve/deltaB read is attacker-skewed.
